content.title: About
content.content: Bread, whole grain white, toasted is a whole‑grain white bread made from wheat flour that has been lightly toasted to a golden crust. It retains the characteristic aroma of toasted bread while staying soft inside and providing the nutrients of whole grain.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain bread contains all parts of the grain: bran, germ and endosperm.
Toasting enhances aroma and creates a crispier crust.
In many cultures toasted bread is used as a base for open‑face sandwiches and snacks.
Thermal processing can slightly reduce some vitamin levels but preserves most dietary fiber.
Bread is often served with butter, cheese, or avocado to boost flavor and nutrition.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The bread supplies iron, magnesium and zinc, important for blood formation and immunity.

items.title: Lower glycemic index than white bread
items.content: Whole‑grain bread raises blood sugar more slowly, beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of fiber and complex carbs helps you feel full longer.

items.title: Wheat allergy or celiac disease
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some toasted breads contain added salt; monitor intake if you watch sodium.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While less calorie‑dense than white bread, portions should still be moderate.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Certain brands may include preservatives or flavor enhancers that not everyone tolerates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted whole‑grain bread works well for open‑face sandwiches, avocado toast, cheese melts, spreads or as a side for soups. Lightly brush with olive oil or use as a crunchy topping for casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box. For longer storage, freeze slices and toast them directly from frozen.
